reject: the person or thing that is rejected or set aside as inferior in quality
rejection: (medicine) an immunological response that refuses to accept substances or organisms that are recognized as foreign
rejoicing: joyful and proud especially because of triumph or success
the utterance of sounds expressing great joy
rejoinder: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)
(law) a pleading made by a defendant in response to the plaintiff's replication
rejuvenation: the phenomenon of vitality and freshness being restored
the act of restoring to a more youthful condition
rejuvenate: cause (a stream or river) to erode, as by an uplift of the land
return to life; get or give new life or energy
